messages:
sandeep: Heads-up — telemetry-store under eng-platform started dropping request logs around 02:12 UTC, disk at ~94%. Looks like recent debug canary increased request/response capture size. Need a quick hotfix to avoid losing audit traces.

maria: Ugh. Which stream is the culprit — full req/resp bodies or attachments?

sandeep: Mostly full req/resp bodies for canary routes (/v1/debug/*). Attachments are small. Suspect we kept sample rate at 1.0 for those routes while rolling.

ops-bot: [ALERT] telemetry-store.disk_usage=94.3% | node=telemetry-prod-3 | action_required=true

jeff: Can we flip the sampling for just the debug routes to 0.01 for now? That should free up a lot of space fast.

sandeep: Yeah propose patch: set route sampling override for /v1/debug/* to 1% and strip request.body.full and response.body.full fields at ingest for 24h. Will need console toggle and a rollback plan.

tia: Quick question on PII — stripping full bodies will remove evidence for some audit cases. Are we sure we can do a temporary backfill later if compliance asks?

maria: We should keep hashed identifiers and metadata (user_id_hashed, request_id, timestamp) so auditability isn't completely lost. Agree to drop full text for now.

sandeep: Implementation plan: 1) push runtime config to lower sample_rate for debug routes; 2) deploy scrub transform that replaces request.body.full with "[redacted]" and keeps request.body.meta.*; 3) monitor console telemetry for error spikes. Target 10m for change and 30m observation.

jeff: Sounds good. For (2) can we use the existing redaction lambda? quick snippet: ```
PATCH /config/routes
{
  "path": "/v1/debug/*",
  "sampling": 0.01,
  "transform": {
    "strip_fields": ["request.body.full","response.body.full"],
    "keep_prefix": ["request.body.meta","response.meta"]
  }
}
```

lena: @sandeep please include a note in rollout channel and tag support; also create a short dashboard panel for dropped logs and retained key fields so we can answer compliance. I'll own the dashboard.

sandeep: On it — will post rollout note and a brief canary SOP. If disk doesn’t drop to <80% in 30m we escalate to snapshot-and-truncate.

ops-bot: [INFO] planned-config-change by sandeep scheduled at 1678890300 | change_id=cfg-20230314-telemetry-hotfix

maria: thumbs up. After stabilization we should schedule a controlled backfill job that re-ingests full bodies from temporary ephemeral store (if retention policy allows) — but only after sign-off from security.

sandeep: Agreed. I'll file a short follow-up RFC for backfill/backstop and call out required KPIs (disk usage, sample retention, auditability matrix).
